DEFINITION

FREQUENCY - The higher the frequency, more charge will pass a given point during a given time. Since more charge movement results in greater current, capacitive reactance (Xc) decreases as frequency increases.

CAPACITANCE - The greater the capacitance, the more stored charge. Applying AC voltage causes charge to move from one plate to another resulting in the flow of charge. Since a greater charge increases current, capacitive reactance (Xc) decreases as capacitance increases.

DEFINITION

FREQUENCY - The higher the frequency, the more electrons pass a given point during a given time. Since more electron movement results in greater current flow, capacitive reactance (Xc) decreases as frequency increases.

CAPACITANCE - The greater the capacitance, the more stored electrons. Applying AC voltage causes the electrons to move from one plate to another resulting in current flow. Since a greater number of electrons increases current flow, capacitive reactance (Xc) decreases as capacitance increases.
